newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai mills buy August soymeal, corn covered.
newsitem.headline: Thai mills buy August soymeal, corn covered.

text.p: Thailand's animal feed industry was seeking August cargoes of soymeal to meet near-term demand while covering for tariff-free corn was said to be nearly complete, trade sources said on Tuesday.
The Soymeal Traders and Importers Association was said to have bought 22,500 tonnes of Argentine/Brazil soymealfor August shipment at $313.29 per tonne c&f Bangkok.
One major feedmill made enquiries but has not placed orders so far, they said.
"There are a lot of supplies of soybean and soymeal coming onto the market now. Buyers can afford to wait for the right prices," said a trader.
Soybean, meal and pellets imports due between May and June are estimated around 300,000 tonnes.
Soymeal on the local market edged down to 9.55-9.90 baht ($0.36) a kg from 9.85-10.10 baht last week.

Corn buying slowed as the zero-tariff quota of 200,000 tonnes was almost used up. One trade house was said to have bought 25,000 tonnes of Argentine corn in transit over the week but cancelled an earlier consignment of 30,000 tonnes bought at origin. The cancellation was made as the firm was concerned that the imports would not arrive here by June 30, the deadline for zero-tariff corn delivery.
The vessel Mountain Pentel is expected to arrive with product by mid-June, they said. Chareon Pokphand's consignments of 67,500 tonnes of Argentine corn were expected to arrive later this week.
The c&f corn market is expected to be calm soon as the government rejected a plea by the feed industry to increase the tariff-free quota by an additional 100,000 tonnes.
The domestic corn price was steady at 4.80 baht a kg in a featureless market, traders said. --Anchalee Koetsawang (662) 652-0642
